content.body:
The QF 17 pounder began development as soon as the military began to realize that the QF 6 pdr would be made obsolete by the heavily armored tanks already in development in Germany. Built on an extremely large split-fork trail with an enormous gun shield, the 17 pdr proved to be one of the most exceptional and hard-hitting anti-tank guns of the entire second world war. It would go on to become the best British AT gun of all. It found its way onto a myriad of tracked vehicles, both self-propelled ATG's and tanks like the famous Firefly variant of the ubiquitous Sherman.
This gun is a big, big hitter that can hit enemies at 2,000 m and beyond. It fires a very flat shot, so first round hits are common. Recoil forces are high, so you may need to exercise skill at long range targets. You don't need to think too much about where to hit an enemy tank with a gun firing a 17 pound armor-piercing projectile at nearly 900 meters a second. Pretty much any impact will do the job until you get to the further ranges.
You might have some issues at long range with a Tiger's mantlet if the angle of impact is poor, but in such cases you will be at an angle where the opportunity to hit the target in its weaker side armor is now favorable. If you struggle to score with a QF 17 pdr you need to hand in your ATG license, because this is the biggest hitting ATG in the game, period.
CREW POSITIONS: 1 Commander 2 Gunner
